channel.title: IngestThis
channel.description: Articles, tutorials, and resources for Data Engineers, Scientists, Analysts, and Architects.

item.title: Building Agent Telemetry Tables in Iceberg That Survive an Audit
item.description: A practical guide to building agent decision traces in Apache Iceberg that support audit reconstruction, governance review, and cost attribution across sessions.

item.title: When the Query Optimizer Starts Managing Its Own Materializations
item.description: Autonomous materialized view management replaces quarterly review meetings with workload-driven scoring, and it's essential when AI agents generate unpredictable query patterns.

item.title: Why AI Agents Fail on Raw Data, and What to Give Them Instead
item.description: Agents fail on raw lake data because business rules live in people's heads. Data products with semantic contracts fix this at the source.

item.title: Why Iceberg V4 Wants to Retire Equality Deletes, and What Streaming Teams Should Do About It
item.description: Equality deletes made streaming upserts into Iceberg practical at the cost of read performance. V4 proposes retiring them in favor of deletion vectors with an async conversion path.

item.title: Surviving Commit Conflicts When Dozens of Writers Hit the Same Iceberg Table
item.description: Commit conflicts multiply with writer count, and AI agents introduce unpredictable write patterns. Here's how to diagnose, tune, and architect around Iceberg's optimistic concurrency.

item.title: Wiring an AI Agent to Apache Polaris with the Model Context Protocol
item.description: The catalog is the right attachment point for AI agents working against a lakehouse. Here's how to wire the official Polaris MCP Server and add the read path it deliberately leaves out.

item.title: The Parquet Versioning Problem, and Why Iceberg Cares About It
item.description: Parquet files have a version field that doesn't reliably signal feature requirements. A new versioning discipline is coming, borrowing from Iceberg's format version model.

item.title: Governing What Agents Cost You
item.description: Agents break the four assumptions analytics platforms were built on. A practical guide to identity, budgets, semantic layers, caching, and instrumentation for agent workloads.

item.title: Every AI Model Family That Matters in Mid-2026
item.description: A full survey of the AI model landscape in mid-2026: frontier families, open-weight labs, local inference, specialists, and how to build a routing layer instead of a dependency.

item.title: Freshness Is a Contract, Not a Note on a Dashboard
item.description: Data freshness needs to become an engineering contract with a measurable value, an owner, and consequences. How to decompose lag, make freshness queryable, and keep agents honest.

item.title: The Apache Iceberg Market in the Middle of 2026
item.description: A survey of the Apache Iceberg market in July 2026: the state of the specification, platform support, the acquisition wave, the catalog contest, and how to evaluate real Iceberg support.

item.title: The Whole Lakehouse Fits on Your Laptop Now
item.description: Consumer hardware, columnar formats, single-node engines, and the Iceberg REST catalog crossed a threshold: a large share of cluster work now runs locally against the same governed tables.

item.title: Iceberg's Next Version Depends on Decisions Being Made in Parquet
item.description: The Iceberg and Parquet specifications are co-evolving. Several of the most consequential Iceberg v4 proposals are waiting on Parquet work, and practitioners should read both dev lists.

item.title: Building a Lakehouse That Stays Inside the Border
item.description: Residency is a storage location. Sovereignty is who can compel access, who operates the systems, and whether you can leave. A practical guide to sovereign lakehouse architecture in 2026.

item.title: Table Maintenance Stopped Being a Product
item.description: Iceberg table maintenance commoditized when every platform started shipping it. What the six operations are, what they cost, and the observability you should keep even when the work is managed.

item.title: The Model Class Enterprise Data Teams Are Not Using Yet
item.description: Tabular foundation models perform supervised learning in a single forward pass with no training run. What they are, where they win, and what they change in the data architecture.

item.title: Three Vendors Are Rebuilding the Path From Transaction to Agent
item.description: Databricks, Snowflake, and SAP are closing the gap between operational databases and analytical platforms through acquisition, betting on different layers of the same five-part architecture.

item.title: What Zero-Copy Actually Costs
item.description: Six architectures share the phrase zero-copy, and they have different costs, failure modes, and governance stories. A walk through federation, virtualization, sharing protocols, and materialization.

item.title: The Filters We Build: Scams, Slop, and the Search for Signal, From Radio Ads to AI
item.description: How every media era from radio to AI forces humanity to build new cognitive filters -- the shield against scams and the sieve for finding signal in an ocean of noise.

item.title: The Breakdown of the Open Lakehouse in 2026: Iceberg, Arrow, Polaris, Parquet, and Ossie, and How to Actually Build One
item.description: A detailed breakdown of the five Apache projects powering the open lakehouse in 2026 -- Parquet, Iceberg, Polaris, Arrow, and Ossie -- and how to build one yourself or use a managed platform.
